We have carbon NMR shifts list. Need number of methyl groups (CH3). Methyl carbons typically appear around 10-30 ppm (alkyl). In list we have shifts: 88.85, 69.70, 68.60, 67.50, 31.31, 28.70, 27.60, 22.65, 18.60, 14.05. The low-field ones: 14.05, 18.60, 22.65, 27.60, 28.70, 31.31 are likely methyl or methylene. Need to differentiate methyl vs methylene. Methyl carbons ~10-30 ppm, methylene ~20-40 maybe overlapping. But we can use typical chemical shift ranges: methyl (CH3) ~10-30 ppm, methylene (CH2) ~20-45 ppm, methine (CH) ~30-55. Hard to differentiate without further info. Could use proton NMR to see number of methyl protons. But we can also infer from carbon count: total 10 carbons. Some are oxygenated (88-69 ppm likely carbons attached to O). The remaining 6 carbons in 14-31 ppm likely aliphatic. Among them, maybe 3 methyls and 3 methylenes? Need to determine number of methyl groups.

We could get proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's request proton NMR.
